paper.title: Lipschitz Bandits: Regret Lower Bounds and Optimal Algorithms

unmapped: finite set of K arms x_1<...<x_K in [0,1] with Lipschitz mean rewards |theta_k - theta_k'| <= L|x_k - x_k'|
settings.definition_quote: We consider a stochastic multi-armed bandit problem where the set of arms is a subset $\{x_1,\ldots,x_K\}$ of the interval $[0,1]$... i.i.d. with Bernoulli distribution of mean $\theta_k$... there exists a positive constant $L$ such that ... $|\theta_k -\theta_{k'}|\le L\times |x_k-x_{k'}|$. We assume that $L$ is also known.

unmapped: finite contexts y_1<...<y_J in [0,1] drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution psi; mean reward Lipschitz jointly in (context, arm) w.r.t. a known metric D
settings.definition_quote: Let $\{y_1,\ldots,y_J\}$ denote the set of possible contexts... There exists $L$ (known to the decision maker) such that ... $| \theta_k(i)-\theta_l(j)|\le L\times {\cal D}((i,k),(j,l))$... The context process is i.i.d.... $\psi$ is unknown to the decision maker.

symbols.C_lin: C(theta): value of LP min sum_k c_k(theta*-theta_k) s.t. sum_i c_i I(theta_i, lambda^k_i) >= 1 for all suboptimal k, with lambda^k_i = max(theta_i, theta* - L|x_k-x_i|)

source.label: th:low
source.quote: Let $\pi\in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm. For any $\theta\in \Theta_L$, we have: \lim\inf_{T\to\infty} {R^\pi(T)\over \log(T)} \ge C(\theta), where $C(\theta)$ is the minimal value of the following optimization problem: \min_{c_k\ge 0} \sum_{k\in {\cal K}^-} c_k (\theta^\star-\theta_k) s.t. \forall k\in {\cal K}^-, \sum_{i} c_i I(\theta_i,\lambda^k_i) \ge 1.

results.notes: Regret defined as T theta* - E[sum rewards] = pseudo-regret. Derived from Graves & Lai (1997).

symbols.C_delta: C^delta(theta), instance constant with C^delta(theta) -> C(theta) (the lower-bound LP value) as delta -> 0+
symbols.delta_an: free analysis parameter delta > 0 (not a failure probability)

conditions: Assumption 1: the solution of the LP defining C(theta) is unique

source.label: th:oslbperf
source.quote: For all $\epsilon>0$, under Assumption \ref{assum:uniqueLP}, the regret achieved under $\pi=\text{OSLB}(\epsilon)$ satisfies: for all $\theta\in \Theta_L$, for all $\delta > 0$ and $T \ge 1$, R^{\pi}(T) \leq C^\delta(\theta) (1+ \epsilon) \log(T) + C_1 \log\log(T) + K^3 \epsilon^{-1} \delta^{-2}+3K\delta^{-2}, where $C^\delta(\theta) \to C(\theta)$, as $\delta \to 0^+$, and $C_1>0$.

results.notes: Paper remarks (not as a formal statement) that this implies limsup R/log T <= C(theta)(1+zeta) for any zeta>0, i.e. asymptotic optimality. The proof restricts delta < gap/2 though statement says all delta>0. Solves an LP each round (polynomial).

bound.regime: 0 < delta < (theta* - max_{k != k*} theta_k)/2, all T >= 1

symbols.I_k_delta: Bernoulli KL divergence kl(theta_k + delta, theta* - delta)

source.label: th:rrucbperf
source.quote: Under CKL-UCB, for all $\theta \in \Theta_{L}$, all $T \geq 1$, all $0 < \delta < (\theta^\star - \max_{k \neq k^\star} \theta_k)/2$, and any suboptimal arm $k \in {\cal K}^{-}$, (i) we have: \EE[ t_k(T) ] \leq \frac{f(T)}{I(\theta_k+\delta, \theta^*-\delta)} + C_1 \log(\log(T)) +  2 \delta^{-2}. with $C_1 \geq 0$ a constant.

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm k (not regret directly).

symbols.beta_k: beta_k(theta) = inf{alpha_0 >= 0 : a_kk alpha_0 + e_k(A, alpha_0) > 1}, defined via the KL matrix A and an LP

source.label: th:rrucbperf
source.quote: (ii) Furthermore, for all $k \in {\cal K}^-$, we have that: \lim \sup_{T \to \infty} \frac{\EE[t_k(T)]}{\log(T)} \leq \beta_k( \theta ). where \beta_k(\theta ) = \inf \{ \alpha_0 \geq 0:  a_{k,k} \alpha_0 + e_k(A,\alpha_0)  > 1    \}.

results.notes: Asymptotic bound on expected pulls of suboptimal arm k. Part (iii) shows beta_k(theta) < 1/kl(theta_k, theta*) under a structural condition (exists k' with 0 < a_kk' < a_kk and zero-pattern condition), i.e. strictly fewer pulls than KL-UCB.
